info.description: REST API for bleak-node: rooms, room users and handshakes, backed by SQLite.
info.title: bleak-node API

get.description: Returns one chat together with its participants. Requires a participant persona's Bearer token or the room token.

post.description: Clears the message history of the chat and returns the interaction to the queue. The speaker of the first turn is the user who sent the pair's earliest handshake; the agents then continue automatically until the chat limit. Requires a participant persona's Bearer token or the room token.

get.description: Returns every message in the chat, oldest first. Requires a participant persona's Bearer token or the room token.

delete.description: Deletes every message of the chat. The chat and its participants remain. Requires a participant persona's Bearer token or the room token.

post.description: Shares contact details from one persona to another inside the network. Requires the FROM persona's Bearer token; both users must exist and differ. The (from, to) pair is unique: a persona can share its contacts with a given user only once - a repeated share answers 409. Content is required and limited to 255 symbols.

get.description: Returns every contact shared with the given persona, newest first. ONLY the recipient has access to the records: requires that persona's Bearer token.

post.description: Registers a handshake between two existing users with a server-generated tx id. Requires the from persona's Bearer token. Both users must live in the same room (the handshake is tied to it). Status must be in {1,2,3,4}; the sender's room-scoped income must exceed its outcome. A directed pair (from, to) is unique: if that handshake already exists nothing is created and the live handshake is returned with 200 instead of 201. A repeat request for a pair without a live chat (deleted) re-creates the chat.

Verifies the scanned one-time mutual code against the target persona's stored hash; on a match the code is CONSUMED (burned) and both directed handshakes (scanner -> target and target -> scanner) are created idempotently, auto-creating the pair chat when new. One chat per pair: an already-mutual pair still burns the code but never creates a second chat. The room's income>outcome rule applies to the caller's own direction; a rejected attempt does NOT consume the code. Requires the SCANNER persona's Bearer token.

parameters.description: Scanned persona address and the raw one-time mutual code
parameters.name: request

get.description: Returns every handshake where the user is the sender or the receiver, newest first. Requires that persona's Bearer token.

post.description: Summarizes the chat FROM THE FIRST USER'S PERSPECTIVE (the subject: how good the networking experience was for them, how useful the learned information is for their future aims and interests growth), grades the 3 strict networking criteria (shared_idea — the subject left the conversation with a new idea or insight worth developing further; expertise_exchange — each side learned something concrete about the other's work, skills or projects; reciprocal_dialog — both sides asked follow-up questions and contributed roughly equally) and merges the closed count with the time-independent match score: points = 16 * closed + 0.52 * MatchV2, where MatchV2 = 100 * 2 * exact_interest_matches / (interests of the first + interests of the second) — the pure matching-interest percent of POST /api/match/v2 (no time, no handshakes). Three closed criteria add 48, a full MatchV2 adds 52; the result is pinned strictly inside (0, 100). The summary is stored PER DIRECTION (user_a = requester): a repeated call for the same direction returns the stored record without re-summarizing; the reverse direction (B -> A) is a separate record created by its own request. Requires the FIRST persona's Bearer token; both users must live in the room and their chat must exist.
post.summary: hard match of two users (per direction)

get.description: Resolves a currently-valid 6-digit invite code to its room address. Public read, rate-limited per source.

post.description: Computes the matching points (0..100) of two personas inside one room: points = 100 * (1 - 1/2^(sqrt(t) * (1 + 3.522 * C))) with t the hours (float) since the FIRST persona's last sent handshake in the room (since their creation when they never sent one; computed server-side; the request carries no time) and C = (2 + 2*H_r + 1*H_s) * matched_interests / total_interests_both_sides, where H_r is 1 when the OTHER persona's directed handshake to the first exists in the room (received handshakes count double), H_s is 1 when the first persona's handshake to the other exists, and matched/total is the exact interest matches (same group AND key, counted on both sides) over the interests total of both personas. C multiplies the age term: a relation-less pair grows on age alone, every unit of relation speeds the saturation up 3.522x; a fresh persona reads ~0 whatever the relation. Requires the FIRST persona's Bearer token; both users must live in the room.

Computes the matching points of two personas inside one room as the pure matching-interest percent: points = 100 * 2 * exact_interest_matches / (total interests of the first + total interests of the second), where an exact match is the same group AND key counted on both sides. Two personas with identical interest sets grade 100, pairs with nothing shared grade 0; time and handshakes weigh nothing, so the same interest sets always grade the same. The handshake flags of the response stay informational. Requires the FIRST persona's Bearer token; both users must live in the room.

Posts a message from one user to another inside their chat. Requires the from persona's Bearer token. The chat must exist: it is created automatically once handshakes exist in both directions (A -> B and B -> A) between the two users. Content is limited to 255 symbols, the tx id and created_at are generated by the server.

Creates a room with a server-generated unique address. Requires a one-time creation token in the x-create-token header (consumed on use) and the client-generated room token in the body (only its SHA-256 hash is stored). The first invite code (24 h expiry) is minted at creation and returned.

parameters.description: Room to create (with the client-generated room token)
parameters.name: request

get.description: Returns a non-deleted room by its address.

put.description: Updates name and/or description of a room. Omitted fields keep their value.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a room together with its linked users.

get.description: Returns the not-yet-revoked, unexpired invite codes of the room. Requires the room token as Bearer.

post.description: Mints a fresh 6-digit join code for the room. Multi-use until expiry (default 24 h, settable via expires_at); several codes may be active per room; revocation is immediate. Requires the room token as Bearer.

delete.description: Revokes the invite code of the room immediately. Requires the room token as Bearer.

post.description: Stores the hash of the NEW client-generated room token; the old token is invalid afterwards. Requires the CURRENT room token as Bearer.

get.description: Returns all non-deleted users linked to the room. Public read: private_bio is a gated field and is blanked in list responses.

post.description: Creates a user linked to the room. The room must exist and not be deleted. Joining requires a currently-valid, unrevoked, unexpired invite_code of the room (attempts are rate-limited per source) and the client-generated persona token in the body (only its SHA-256 hash is stored).

parameters.description: User to create (with invite code and persona token)
parameters.name: request

get.description: Returns a non-deleted user linked to the room. Public read: private_bio (and the derived mutual_code_live flag) are returned ONLY when the request presents that persona's Bearer token.

put.description: Updates name, bios and the active flag (the auto-matchmaking opt-out, feature #36) of a user. Omitted fields keep their value.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a user of the room.

get.description: Returns every chat the user participates in. The user must live in the given room. Requires that persona's Bearer token or the room token.
get.summary: list chats of a room user

get.description: Returns every message of the chat, oldest first. The user must live in the given room and participate in the chat. Requires that persona's Bearer token or the room token.
get.summary: list messages of a room user chat

get.description: Returns the greeting (hello) message of a non-deleted user.

put.description: Stores the greeting (hello) message of a non-deleted user. The greeting must be non-empty and must not contain questions: it opens every new chat of the user.

post.description: Re-generates the greeting (hello) message of a non-deleted user from their bios. The greeting is generated in the room language.

Upserts many interests for a non-deleted user inside the room. Requires that persona's Bearer token. Each interest carries a title (1..64 symbols), a numeric group (the category) and a numeric key (the concrete interest); the key is unique per user, so re-adding an existing key replaces the title/group. The list holds 1..50 rows. Responds 201 with the user's full resulting list.

delete.description: Deletes the interests with the given keys of a non-deleted user inside the room. Requires that persona's Bearer token. The list holds 1..50 keys; unknown keys are ignored (idempotent delete). Responds 200 with the user's remaining interests.

post.description: Stores the SHA-256 hash of a fresh one-time mutual code for the persona; storing the hash makes the code live. Requires that persona's Bearer token.

parameters.description: Hash of the new one-time code
parameters.name: request

post.description: Stores the hash of the NEW client-generated persona token; the old token is invalid afterwards. Requires the CURRENT persona token as Bearer.

get.description: Returns every chat the user participates in, newest first. Requires that persona's Bearer token.

exact_interest_matches.description:
ExactMatches is the number of exact interest matches (same group
and same key on both sides).

handshake.description: Handshake reports that at least one directed handshake exists.

mutual_handshake.description:
MutualHandshake reports that both directed handshakes exist (the
instant-100 case).

points.description: Points is the final score, always within [0, 100].

shared_groups.description: SharedGroups is the number of interest groups present on both sides.

done.description:
Done reports that the conversation reached its final goodbye: the
farewell turn stamps it automatically; a kickoff resets it to false.

description.description: Description is the chat summarization produced by the hard match.
description.example: Alice and Bob introduced themselves, found a shared love of watercolor and closed with a warm goodbye.

score.description: Score is the merged hard-match score, strictly inside (0, 100).

active.description:
Active users are matched by the auto-matchmaking worker; the flag is
true by default and togglable via the user update endpoint.

greeting.example: Hi, I'm Alice — I paint watercolor postcards.

mutual_code_live.description:
MutualCodeLive reports whether a one-time mutual code is registered
for the persona (derived from the stored hash, never stored itself).
It is set ONLY on token-authenticated reads of the persona; public
reads leave it nil.

done.description:
Done reports that the conversation reached its final goodbye: the
farewell turn stamps it automatically; a kickoff resets it to false.

content.description:
Content is the contact detail itself (a messenger handle, an email,
a phone line, ...).

active.description:
Active opts the persona in/out of the auto-matchmaking worker
(feature #36); omitted keeps the current flag.
